title: Streamed function invocation conformance suite for onboarded models
creator: Lena Park
description:
Scope: build a deterministic end-to-end conformance and verification suite that validates streamed function/tool invocation semantics for models added to the catalog. This ticket covers: 1) an automated harness that exercises handshake, chunking, and backpressure semantics across model variants and pinned versions; 2) a set of golden prompts that exercise structured output (JSON/ndjson), multi-tool sequences, and partial-final output transitions; 3) performance profiling hooks to capture per-model p50/p95/p99 latency, token emission throughput, and CPU/GPU utilization during streaming with tool calls; 4) publishing artifacts (conformance badge + perf profile) to the model catalog and onboarding checklist.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals: verify functional compatibility of streaming + function/tool calling for each onboarded model and pinned version, detect and classify failure modes (e.g., truncated JSON, dropped function calls, incorrect tool-arg sequencing), and produce machine-readable conformance results and human-friendly reports for PR reviewers and the model catalog.
- Non-goal: this ticket does not change runtime semantics or add new protocol features; it focuses on verification and reporting.

Acceptance criteria:
- A reproducible test harness (k8s job + local runner) that runs a configurable matrix of: model, version pin, sequence length, tokenization edge-cases, and tool-call topologies.
- A canonical set of 25 test cases covering: handshake race, partial JSON emission, tool-arg streaming, KV-cache warm/cold with streaming, backpressure recovery, and late function-call injection.
- CI step that runs a fast subset on PRs for model onboarding and a nightly full-matrix run that uploads artifacts to the onboarding dashboard.
- Perf profiles generated for each model-version that include p50/p95/p99 token latency, streaming throughput, and memory spike summaries; must be stored as JSONL artifacts linked from the model catalog entry.
- A published conformance badge for models that pass the suite and a failure taxonomy for models that fail (transient vs deterministic behavior).

Test matrix highlights:
- Model axes: small->large variants, float16/quantized variants, and emergence of internal sampler differences.
- Network axes: 0ms/20ms/80ms artificial egress latency to ensure graceful degradation of streaming tool calls.
- Load axes: single-request, burst-10, continuous-100qps simulated bursts to validate KV cache and batching interactions with streaming.

Instrumentation and telemetry:
- Use existing tracing hooks (trace-id injection) to correlate emitted tokens with tool-call events.
- Record token-level timestamps and event markers (handshake_start, first_token, func_call_start, func_arg_chunk, func_return, stream_end).
- Export metrics to telemetry team dashboard: streaming.func_call.latency_ms, streaming.token.emit_rate, streaming.backpressure.count.

Publishing/perf profile format:
- Perf profiles will be JSONL with one line per run: {"model":"...","version":"...","p50_ms":"...","p95_ms":"...","p99_ms":"...","emit_rate_tps":"...","notes":"..."}
- Conformance results will be a small JSON summary and a human-readable html report stored in the onboarding artifacts bucket.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement harness and 10 core test cases (2-week spike).
2) Add full golden set, CI integration, and nightly runs (week 3–4).
3) Publish perf profile uploader and model catalog integration (week 5).
4) Post-mortem and iterate on flaky tests; add to onboarding checklist (week 6).

Risks & mitigations:
- Flaky timing tests: mitigate by using deterministic playback for token emission and configurable network emulation.
- Resource cost of nightly full-matrix runs: implement sampling and short-circuit on deterministic pass to reduce runtime.
- False positives due to model nondeterminism: run each failing case 3x and classify as flake vs deterministic failure.

Links and artifacts:
- Design spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.local/display/INF/Streamed+Function+Invocation+Conformance
- Draft harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/6722
- Nightly artifacts dashboard (internal): https://dashboards.redwood.local/onboarding/streamed-func-conformance

Next steps:
- Spike harness prototype and share early results in FW sync.
- Add required test cases to ticket and assign owners for each case.
- Coordinate with telemetry for metric names and retention.
